A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASAP research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original packing and routing experiments, adaptation results, ablations, and MCTS-based analyses in Section 5 and Appendices C and F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds full-parameter adaptation controls and TSPLIB/CVRPLIB evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposal-selection architecture, two-phase training, MAML option, and selection-only online adaptation are retained. The baseline-derived adaptation loss is clarified; 'Tune All' is an experimental control rather than a replacement for the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F.2.1 adds evaluations on TSPLIB and CVRPLIB Set-X instance populations grouped by size, supplementing the generated routing-distribution tests. This extends benchmark coverage within the retained TSP/CVRP tasks; packing coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 add 'Tune All' counterparts for PCT+ASAP, POMO+ASAP, and INViT-1V+ASAP with MAML. Existing external baselines remain, and the new library evaluations use the previously evaluated routing comparator families.

E3.justification: The new control updates all parameters during adaptation instead of freezing the proposal policy. Table 10 also introduces size-grouped, pre/post-adaptation library evaluations. Existing synthetic settings remain unchanged; the additional packing-data explanation does not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: The added selective-versus-full-tuning ablation directly tests whether freezing the proposal policy benefits adaptation across packing and routing. Existing MAML, ASAP, proposal-size, and MCTS analyses are retained, including v3 Table 10 as v4 Table 11.

E5.justification: Both retain three-seed information in Tables 4 and 5 and the baseline setup. v4 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Matched existing scores remain unchanged, while control and library results are added. Table 1 reports 73.7% discrete ID-Large utilization for Tune All versus the retained 74.2% for selective adaptation. New Table 10 reports a 6.98% post-adaptation TSPLIB gap above 1000 nodes for INViT-1V+ASAP with MAML. These supplement existing results rather than demonstrate version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 and Appendix B's derivations are unchanged. v4 explicitly distinguishes proposal and selection policies in the main-text definition and restates the same-policy assumption already documented in v3 Appendix B; this adds clarification rather than new mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the Satisficing Generalization Edge, ASAP, generalization, and rapid adaptation. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly attributes the generally smaller gains from full-parameter adaptation to likely overfitting on limited online instances. This adds a tentative mechanism explanation; existing qualifications concerning approximate routing ground truth remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly identifies the adaptation loss as inherited from the integrated DRL baseline. Appendix E.1 newly documents removing rotationally redundant item shapes and sampling nonuniform distributions by batch. Hardware, hyperparameter tables, and supplementary-code access statements are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction shifts the stated advantage of DRL over traditional heuristics toward architecture and training-scheme reuse across problems. Appendix E.1 also explicitly distinguishes the packing-data construction from PCT's. The cited-work set otherwise remains stable; updated bibliography entries correspond to the same works.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized introduction and method-explanation edits, swaps the packing and routing related-work subsections, adds experimental discussion and acknowledgments, and updates publication information. The overall narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 10, expands Tables 1 and 2 with Tune All rows, and corrects Table 1's caption to cover 3D-BPP datasets generally. Earlier Tables 10 and 11 become Tables 11 and 12. Figure typography/rendering and page placement receive limited revisions without changing the plotted findings.

improvement.justification: The new full-tuning control directly strengthens evidence for selective adaptation, and the library evaluations broaden empirical support. Loss and packing-data clarifications improve reproducibility. These are useful, limited gains: selective adaptation does not win every control comparison, and benchmark-specific instance selection and adaptation details remain sparse. The revision strengthens the existing paper without substantially changing its method, theory, or conclusions.
